rationale: Block 3 closes the concept of trace elements as metalloenzyme cofactors; dragging each element into its enzyme tests the key pairings.
Block 5 closes the overview of body water compartments, electrolyte distribution and buffer systems; fill-in-the-blank tests recall of the foundational values and terms.
Block 7 closes the iron absorption pathway from lumen to blood; ordering visually distinct stages tests understanding of the sequential steps and the role of each transporter.
Block 12 closes the section on iron and copper disorders; recalling the key differentiating proteins and mutations separates IDA from ACD and identifies the hereditary overload states.
Block 14 closes the section on calcium, phosphate and magnesium disorders; identifying the clinical signs of tetany from prose tests recognition of the key examination findings.
Block 17 closes the acid-base disorders section with a five-step blood-gas interpretation method; ordering the steps tests the learner's ability to apply the systematic approach.
